entry.title: The Fastest Academic Supercomputer in the U.S. | Horizon Supercomputer at UT Austin

author.name: The University of Texas at Austin

media:group.media:title: The Fastest Academic Supercomputer in the U.S. | Horizon Supercomputer at UT Austin
media:group.media:description:
Horizon, the most powerful academic supercomputer in the United States, is now open to its first researchers at the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) at The University of Texas at Austin.
Funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation, Horizon is the centerpiece of the NSF Leadership-Class Computing Facility. Its first phase runs on 4,000 NVIDIA GPUs and ranks No. 24 on the November 2026 TOP500 list of the world's fastest supercomputers. It's built for both AI and simulation, and it runs simulations 10 times faster than Frontera, the system it replaces. With Horizon, TACC now has nearly 5,500 GPUs, the most computing power at any university in the country.
Researchers will use Horizon on problems too big, too complex, or too risky to test in a lab, such as tracing how a flash flood moves through a Hill Country watershed, stress-testing the power grid before a winter storm, and speeding up treatments for deadly diseases. Its work will span medicine, earthquake science, quantum materials, astronomy, and more.
Horizon was built with Dell Technologies, NVIDIA, and VAST Data, and it's housed in a new liquid-cooled data center in Round Rock, Texas. CPU servers will be added in early 2027, which will push its performance even higher.
Read the full story: https://news.utexas.edu/2026/11/17/horizon-opens-to-early-users-americas-most-powerful-academic-supercomputer-begins-serving-science/
